newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Cavallo vows silence, recommends Menem dump aides.
newsitem.headline: Cavallo vows silence, recommends Menem dump aides.

text.p: Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo promised to limit his denunciations of corruption to the courts -- but went out recommending that President Carlos Menem get rid of three senior aides.

Cavallo, sacked in July, told La Nacion newspaper in an interview published Tuesday: "Friends have told me my public actions in recent weeks have created unease and I want to avoid that; so I have decided not to speak anymore."

He has accused Interior Minister Carlos Corach and Justice Minister Elias Jassan of manipulating judges and covering up graft, and Menem's Chief of Staff Alberto Kohan of ignoring bribes paid to a state bank by IBM's Argentine unit.
The three have denied the allegations and Corach has said he will sue Cavallo for defamation.
The others are mulling legal action.

The row was already weighing on markets and worrying local business leaders when Clarin newspapers quoted Cavallo as saying, "If the Argentine economy withstood a change of minister, it can withstand a change of president."

Cavallo has denied this was a direct attack on Menem, and said: "It's not my intention to scare or worry the public. So since they have gone on about me speaking without proof, I have decided to speak only before the courts."
However, the combative Harvard-trained economist, spending two days at home between lectures abroad "to earn a living", took another swipe at Corach, Jassan and Kohan.
"If the president got rid of these officials, bonds and shares would rise spectacularly," he told La Nacion.

He denied his campaign is doing more harm than good: "The fact that an Argentine citizen who was economy minister has the courage to stand up to officials as I did should bring country risk down, not increase it."

"I hope people who want to help wipe out organized crime in Argentina will show the courage I have. It can't be that only the cases I denounce, or in which I produce evidence, are uncovered," Cavallo said.
